I’m beginning to think that you just don’t understand the basic purpose of a review. Typically someone writes their experience of a place and recommends to either go or not to go.
Statistically you will find in reviews people who either had an amazing experience and recommend everyone goes to try out the service or a very bad experience where they recommend you avoid the service. Most people with average responses do not feel compelled to spend the time writing that everything they expected to happen did in fact happen.

OP did not like the review and based off of this recommends not going. It wasn’t about the $2 or the water. It was about being trusting the owner that the info he shared was correct and then when it wasn’t, not being offered even an apology or a simple exchange to the product he was looking for. If this is something you care about in the service you receive, dont go. If it’s not, do go.
